plain: The bank names a number, and its own filed spreadsheet has a line with that name. We can look it up and compare.
example: JPMorganChase had $4.4 trillion in assets and $362.4 billion in stockholders' equity as of December 31, 2025

plain: The number is a movement, not an amount. Nobody files a movement — checking it means looking up two years and subtracting.
example: Noninterest expense was $95.6 billion, up 4%, driven by higher compensation expense

plain: The figure covers one division or product. The bank did file it and an auditor did sign it — but the SEC's public download hands back whole-bank totals only and drops the by-division detail.
example: Net charge-offs were $9.8 billion, up $1.2 billion, predominantly driven by Wholesale and Card Services

plain: The right kind of number to look up, but nothing in the filed spreadsheet is named that. Sometimes it genuinely was never filed; sometimes our search missed it — so this band is an upper bound.
example: Equity Markets revenue was $13.3 billion, up 33%

plain: Not a filed number at all — someone calculated it, sometimes with their own private recipe. There is no filed value to compare it to.
example: JPMorganChase reported net income of $57.0 billion for 2025, down 2%, earnings per share of $20.02, ROE of 17% and ROTCE of 20%
